artifacts.summary: 10-phase implementation plan converting ~94 hand-rolled state.json write sites across 46 source-store files to state-write.sh, plus a new permanently-wired lint-state-writer-boundary.sh; explicitly resolves the commands/*.md scope-boundary question as INCLUDE.

memory_candidates.content: When a task's declared state.json file_scope disagrees with the breadth stated in its own description body or VERIFICATION BAR, the description body wins. file_scope is documented in rules/state-management.md and context/reference/state-management-schema.md as descriptive/anticipated, set at creation time, never filesystem-validated, and used only for lock-overlap detection -- it is not a contract boundary that authorizes or forbids edits. The decisive test is whether the narrower reading leaves the task's own verification bar unsatisfiable: if honoring file_scope means the stated bar can never pass, the bar (not file_scope) defines the real scope. A planner MUST state the inclusion/exclusion decision explicitly with reasons rather than silently narrowing or widening, and any residual left out needs an enumerated, individually-evidenced exclusion list rather than an unqualified 'zero hits' claim.
